title: GPU pool livelock resolution and adaptive admission plan
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Follow-up ticket from a hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion incident that resulted in long queue build-up, tenant livelock where repeated admission attempts amplified queue depth, and cascading throttles. This ticket consolidates actionable engineering steps, telemetry gaps, and verification experiments to reduce recurrence risk and improve graceful degradation under bursty multi-tenant load.
root_cause_summary: A combination of aggressive tenant retries, insufficient admission normalization across tenant weights, and autoscaler hysteresis settings caused slow reaction to demand spikes. Prefix and KV cache cold starts amplified per-request GPU time, increasing slot occupancy. Observability lacked per-tenant queue-depth histograms and spike-correlated prewarm metrics, which delayed detection and mitigation.
action_items: Implement tenant admission score normalization: cap per-tenant admission attempts and apply exponential backoff on failed admission to prevent livelock
Add a lightweight fast-fail path for requests that exceed queue-depth thresholds with a deterministic retry-after header for clients
Tune autoscaler hysteresis and priming: lower scale-up detection window for short spikes and implement short-lived prewarm instances to absorb sudden bursts
Expose per-pool and per-tenant queue-depth percentile metrics (p50/p90/p99) and tokenized request size distribution to the Console
Instrument and persist KV-cache warmness metric per-model and per-shard to drive prewarm heuristics
Create a tenant admission score audit log (immutable) to replay admission decisions during post-incident analysis
Build a synthetic tenant surge harness (k6 + model-simulator) that reproduces observed burst patterns and validates mitigations before rollout
Implement a staged rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%) for admission changes with automatic rollback on error or latency regression
Author runbook snippets for SRE to triage and perform emergency manual admission caps and pool rebinds
Add regression tests to CI that assert queue growth rates under shaped synthetic load to prevent reintroduction
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Kaur: Created ticket after alignment with incident PM and SRE. Initial action-item brainstorm captured.
2025-02-12 Liam O'Neill: Spike harness prototype committed to feature/eng/queue-harness branch (see links). Found that 60% of surge requests came from 3 tenants.
2025-02-15 SRE rotation (Marcos Alvarez): Confirmed autoscaler did not trigger until 90s into the event due to current smoothing window. Proposed lowering smoothing to 30s for critical pools.
2025-02-18 Design review (Frances Chen): Noted Console UI requirements for new per-tenant histograms; requested mockups and filter-by-tenant support.
2025-02-20 Engineering: Implemented admission backoff prototype behind feature flag; running in internal canary on staging for 48h.
2025-02-24 Observability: Dashboard updated with provisional queue-depth percentiles for staging pools. Need to index by tenant id for hosted customers.
2025-02-28 Liam O'Neill: Moved ticket to In Progress; prioritizing admission normalization, telemetry gaps, and synthetic tests. Next sync planned 2025-03-03.
decision_logs: Decision 2025-02-14: Prefer admission-side throttles over aggressive eviction because eviction causes more downstream client errors and cache thrash.
Decision 2025-02-21: Autoscaler hysteresis change will be guarded by safety flags and gradual rollout; priming instances will be billed to a short-lived buffer to measure cost impact.
Decision 2025-02-25: Fast-fail responses must include Retry-After and standardized error codes for SDKs to surface to customers.
Decision 2025-02-27: Security review required for admission audit log because it contains tenant identifiers; SSO/HSM access gating plan to be provided.
